  "concordance_definition": "The study compared tenocyte morphology, proliferation rate, wound healing speed, and gene expression of four animal models (mouse, rat, sheep, horse) to human tenocytes under healthy and inflamed conditions to determine similarities and differences among species, using Mahalanobis distances and Principal Component Analysis to assess multivariate dissimilarity in gene expression.",
  "limitations_stated": [
    "No single animal model perfectly recapitulates the clinical realm.",
    "Species differences in disease pathophysiology, comorbidities, and outcome measures.",
    "Lack of in-depth validation studies for animal models beyond structural and biomechanical similarities for tendinopathy.",
    "No species has been established as the gold standard for tendinopathy research.",
    "The diversity of human patients and symptoms is unlikely fully represented in highly inbred rodents.",
    "Humanized models cannot replicate the complexity of human disease.",
    "The choice of animal models is frequently based on convention, financial and practical considerations rather than scientific evidence.",
    "Species may differ in critical aspects and assumed similarities are rarely empirically demonstrated.",
    "No animal model sufficiently emulates human tenocytes’ cellular and molecular features and response to inflammation to be considered the gold-standard.",
    "Peculiarities, strengths, and weaknesses of model species need to be accounted for in study design, analysis, and interpretation."
  ],
  "funding_conflict": null,
  "key_numbers": [
    "90% of new treatment strategies fail translation from basic science to clinic.",
    "52% of failures are due to inefficiency, 24% due to unsafety.",
    "Tendinopathy affects 25% of the adult population and accounts for 30-50% of all sport injuries.",
    "Achilles tendon routinely experiences loads up to 12.5 times body weight.",
    "Tendinopathy costs an estimated annual expense of $30 billion.",
    "Human tenocytes measured 177.8 ± 40.1 μm in length and 20.2 ± 4.4 μm in width.",
    "Mouse tenocytes measured 163.7 ± 23.6 μm in length and 19.4 ± 3.3 μm in width.",
    "Rat tenocytes measured 182.5 ± 26.6 μm in length and 24.2 ± 8.0 μm in width.",
    "Sheep tenocytes measured 206.3 ± 45.5 μm in length and 28.9 ± 8.5 μm in width.",
    "Horse tenocytes measured 193.2 ± 8.4 μm in length and 15.4 ± 1.4 μm in width.",
    "Equine tenocytes had the highest proliferation rates under healthy conditions.",
    "Murine cells had the lowest proliferation rates under healthy conditions.",
    "Human tenocytes exhibited the second lowest proliferation capacity.",
    "Rat tenocytes showed the fastest wound healing under healthy conditions (90.08% ± 8.01% gap closure at 48h).",
    "Human tenocytes showed 86.25% ± 2.47% gap closure at 48h.",
    "Mouse tenocytes showed the slowest wound healing (51.49% ± 10.23% gap closure at 48h).",
    "Healthy tenocytes of all four species show significant differences to humans in expression of Col1, MMP13, and COX2.",
    "No significant differences to humans were seen in MMP1 expression for any species.",
    "Overall gene expression of human tenocytes was most similar to murine under healthy conditions.",
    "Overall gene expression of human tenocytes was most similar to equine under transient inflammation.",
    "Overall gene expression of human tenocytes was most similar to ovine under constant inflammation.",
    "Horses provided the best match to humans for ECM remodelling genes (MMPs).",
    "Rats provided the worst match to humans for ECM remodelling genes (MMPs).",
    "Rat tenocytes most closely approximated human tendon cells in inflammatory mediator expression.",
    "PC1 explained 36% of the variance in gene expression data.",
    "PC3 explained 14% of the variance in gene expression data."
  ]
